title: The Edges of the Wave
endLine: The ECG moves only while a boundary between cells travels.

scenes.tts: In the first film, one ventricular cell held its plateau. Now nearly every ventricular cell is up there together, far above rest. Yet the tracing on the skin is flat. Why?
scenes.narration: In the first film, one ventricular cell held its plateau. Now nearly every ventricular cell is up there together, far above rest. Yet the tracing on the skin is flat. Why?
scenes.caption: In the first film, one ventricular cell held its plateau. Now nearly every ventricular cell is up there together, far above rest. Yet the tracing on the skin is flat. Why?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). Carry the first film's colours: single-cell voltage trace WHITE; excited cells on their plateau GOLD; resting cells BLUE. New: the ECG trace bright GREEN; the moving boundary MAGENTA. Layout: TOP HALF, a horizontal strip of ten ventricular muscle cells joined end to end, filling the frame width, with a chest electrode icon above its centre (no plus or minus sign on it). BOTTOM HALF, a long ECG paper with the GREEN trace drawn left to right. Small tag 'schematic' at bottom right all film. Do not name any lead. Motion: the first film's WHITE plateau trace appears in a small inset at top left. All ten cells fade from BLUE to GOLD together. The GREEN trace runs dead level. White text: 'All depolarized. Flat. Why?'
Title 'The Edges of the Wave' fades in for 2 s above the strip. The question text fades out. The GOLD cells shimmer and the GREEN trace keeps running level.

scenes.tts: A natural guess says the E C G is all the action potentials added up. But that sum would stay high right through the plateau.
scenes.narration: A natural guess says the ECG is all the action potentials added up. But that sum would stay high right through the plateau.
scenes.caption: A natural guess says the ECG is all the action potentials added up. But that sum would stay high right through the plateau.
scenes.visual: Ten small WHITE plateau traces lift out of the cells and stack into one tall WHITE sum curve on the ECG paper, staying high across the plateau, labelled 'sum of cells'. The level GREEN trace runs beneath it, labelled 'real trace'. On 'plateau' a white cross lands on the WHITE sum curve and it fades.

scenes.tts: An electrode on the chest cannot record any one cell's action potential. What reaches it is current in the fluid around the cells. That current flows only where neighboring cells differ in voltage.
scenes.narration: An electrode on the chest cannot record any one cell's action potential. What reaches it is current in the fluid around the cells. That current flows only where neighboring cells differ in voltage.
scenes.caption: An electrode on the chest cannot record any one cell's action potential. What reaches it is current in the fluid around the cells. That current flows only where neighboring cells differ in voltage.
scenes.visual: The cells return to BLUE, all at rest. Camera eases in on the electrode and the thin band of fluid along the strip. Between two cells, one briefly turned GOLD beside one BLUE, faint MAGENTA current loops appear in the fluid and reach toward the electrode. When both cells match in colour the loops vanish. Label: 'different voltages, current flows'.

scenes.tts: Picture a strip of muscle with a wave halfway along it. Behind the wave, cells sit on their plateau. Ahead, they are still at rest.
scenes.narration: Picture a strip of muscle with a wave halfway along it. Behind the wave, cells sit on their plateau. Ahead, they are still at rest.
scenes.caption: Picture a strip of muscle with a wave halfway along it. Behind the wave, cells sit on their plateau. Ahead, they are still at rest.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole strip. The left five cells are GOLD, labelled 'plateau'; the right five are BLUE, labelled 'rest'. A soft bright line marks the junction between cells five and six.

scenes.tts: At the boundary, positive charge crosses gap junctions, and the circuit closes through the fluid outside. So the boundary acts like a small battery, travelling with the wave.
scenes.narration: At the boundary, positive charge crosses gap junctions, and the circuit closes through the fluid outside. So the boundary acts like a small battery, travelling with the wave.
scenes.caption: At the boundary, positive charge crosses gap junctions, and the circuit closes through the fluid outside. So the boundary acts like a small battery, travelling with the wave.
scenes.visual: Small white plus signs pass through a gap junction from the GOLD cell into the BLUE cell. A MAGENTA loop closes around the junction through the fluid. The junction condenses into a MAGENTA battery icon labelled 'moving boundary'. It slides rightward along the strip, turning each BLUE cell GOLD as it passes. While it moves, the GREEN trace makes a schematic deflection; when it reaches the far end, the trace returns level. No narration or label about up or down.
No narration; motion continues. The MAGENTA battery travels the full length of the strip, turning each BLUE cell GOLD, and the GREEN trace moves only while it travels, then runs level.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. The E C G never shows a cell's voltage. It shows only differences between cells, so it sees the edges of waves.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. The ECG never shows a cell's voltage. It shows only differences between cells, so it sees the edges of waves.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. The ECG never shows a cell's voltage. It shows only differences between cells, so it sees the edges of waves.
scenes.visual: Three frames of the same strip side by side, each above its own piece of GREEN trace: all BLUE with a level trace; half GOLD and half BLUE with the MAGENTA battery and a moving trace; all GOLD with a level trace. Large white text: 'It sees the edges.'
No narration; motion continues. A highlight passes across the three frames in turn while each GREEN trace repeats its own behaviour.

scenes.tts: Now read one beat. At first every cell is at rest, so the trace is flat. Then depolarization spreads across the atria. That moving edge is the P wave.
scenes.narration: Now read one beat. At first every cell is at rest, so the trace is flat. Then depolarization spreads across the atria. That moving edge is the P wave.
scenes.caption: Now read one beat. At first every cell is at rest, so the trace is flat. Then depolarization spreads across the atria. That moving edge is the P wave.
scenes.visual: The strip morphs into a simple outline heart with atria above and ventricles below, all BLUE, a MAGENTA boundary ready at the sinoatrial node. The ECG paper clears for one schematic beat. The GREEN pen runs level, then the MAGENTA edge sweeps across the atria, turning them GOLD as the pen draws a small rounded bump labelled 'P'.
No narration; motion continues. The atria glow evenly GOLD and the GREEN pen settles after the P wave.

scenes.tts: Next the wave crawls through the A V node and the bundle of His. An edge is still travelling. So should the trace move here?
scenes.narration: Next the wave crawls through the AV node and the bundle of His. An edge is still travelling. So should the trace move here?
scenes.caption: Next the wave crawls through the AV node and the bundle of His. An edge is still travelling. So should the trace move here?
scenes.visual: A small MAGENTA dot creeps down through a narrow path between atria and ventricles, labelled 'AV node, bundle of His'. The GREEN pen pauses at the point just after P, not yet drawing. Question card in white: 'An edge moves. Does the trace?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: the small MAGENTA dot pulses in place and the GREEN pen waits. Do not draw the next piece of trace.

scenes.tts: It stays nearly flat. Those structures are too small for their boundary to register at the skin. The more tissue a boundary spans, the bigger the deflection.
scenes.narration: It stays nearly flat. Those structures are too small for their boundary to register at the skin. The more tissue a boundary spans, the bigger the deflection.
scenes.caption: It stays nearly flat. Those structures are too small for their boundary to register at the skin. The more tissue a boundary spans, the bigger the deflection.
scenes.visual: The card dissolves. The MAGENTA dot finishes its crawl while the GREEN pen draws a nearly level segment labelled 'PR segment'. Beside the heart, two MAGENTA batteries appear, one tiny and one large, each with a bar showing deflection size in proportion.

scenes.tts: Then the wave races through the Purkinje network and crosses the ventricles. That large moving edge is the Q R S complex. Its width is the crossing time.
scenes.narration: Then the wave races through the Purkinje network and crosses the ventricles. That large moving edge is the QRS complex. Its width is the crossing time.
scenes.caption: Then the wave races through the Purkinje network and crosses the ventricles. That large moving edge is the QRS complex. Its width is the crossing time.
scenes.visual: A broad MAGENTA edge sweeps quickly through the ventricles, turning them GOLD. The GREEN pen draws a tall narrow QRS complex in step with it. A small white bracket under the complex, labelled 'crossing time', marks its width.
No narration; motion continues. The MAGENTA edge fades as the last ventricular cells turn GOLD and the crossing-time bracket glows under the QRS complex.

scenes.tts: Now nearly every ventricular cell is on its plateau. With no edge left to travel, the S T segment is flat, or nearly so.
scenes.narration: Now nearly every ventricular cell is on its plateau. With no edge left to travel, the ST segment is flat, or nearly so.
scenes.caption: Now nearly every ventricular cell is on its plateau. With no edge left to travel, the ST segment is flat, or nearly so.
scenes.visual: The ventricles glow evenly GOLD, with no MAGENTA anywhere. The small WHITE plateau trace from the opening returns in the inset, high and steady, while the GREEN pen draws a nearly level segment labelled 'ST'. The text from the hook returns briefly: 'All depolarized. Flat.'
No narration; motion continues. The ventricles shimmer evenly GOLD, the WHITE inset trace holds high, and the GREEN pen keeps running nearly level.

scenes.tts: Recovery makes one more edge. Different regions repolarize at different times, which forms a broad, slow boundary. That boundary is the T wave.
scenes.narration: Recovery makes one more edge. Different regions repolarize at different times, which forms a broad, slow boundary. That boundary is the T wave.
scenes.caption: Recovery makes one more edge. Different regions repolarize at different times, which forms a broad, slow boundary. That boundary is the T wave.
scenes.visual: Patches of the ventricles fade from GOLD back to BLUE at different moments, leaving a soft, wide MAGENTA band between them. Show no arrow for the band's direction. The GREEN pen draws a broad rounded wave labelled 'T', then runs level as all cells reach BLUE.
No narration; motion continues. The last GOLD patches fade to BLUE and the GREEN pen runs level after the T wave.

scenes.tts: The Q T interval runs from the start of Q R S to the end of T. A longer plateau means a longer Q T.
scenes.narration: The QT interval runs from the start of QRS to the end of T. A longer plateau means a longer QT.
scenes.caption: The QT interval runs from the start of QRS to the end of T. A longer plateau means a longer QT.
scenes.visual: A white bracket spans the beat from the start of QRS to the end of T, labelled 'QT'. The WHITE single-cell trace from the first film slides down and lines up under the bracket. Its plateau stretches slightly (schematic), and the bracket and T wave move right with it.

scenes.tts: So the skin learns little from a heart in agreement. All at rest, or all on the plateau, the line stays level. Only moving disagreement writes the beat.
scenes.narration: So the skin learns little from a heart in agreement. All at rest, or all on the plateau, the line stays level. Only moving disagreement writes the beat.
scenes.caption: So the skin learns little from a heart in agreement. All at rest, or all on the plateau, the line stays level. Only moving disagreement writes the beat.
scenes.visual: The heart replays one full beat at gentle speed: each MAGENTA edge lights as the GREEN pen moves, and when the heart is evenly BLUE, or when the ventricles are evenly GOLD with the atria back to BLUE, the pen runs level. The finished beat stays on the paper with P, QRS and T lit.

End card over the dimmed world, large white text, centred: 'The ECG moves only while a boundary between cells travels.' A faint MAGENTA edge keeps sweeping through the heart behind it, and the GREEN trace keeps running.
